title: Zolotarev's Lemma — The Cycle Producer and Units-Form Identity for the Permutation-Sign Route to QR
description: The permutation-sign (Zolotarev) route to quadratic reciprocity, machine-checked in Lean 4. Supplies the producer lemma Mathlib lacks — left-multiplication by a generator of a finite group is a single cycle — derives the Zolotarev sign computation sign(mulLeft (g^k)) = (-1)^k, proves the Euler-side crux that a primitive root of (ZMod p)ˣ raised to (p-1)/2 equals -1, and assembles the units-form Zolotarev headline legendreSym p u = sign(mulLeft u) for u : (ZMod p)ˣ. The exact OQ-pinned field statement using mulLeft₀ on ZMod p (via the units→field sign bridge) and Milestone 2 (reciprocity from the grid-transpose sign) remain open.

MACHINE-CHECKED across three Docker-recovered sessions: S14 (2026-06-15, #24738) verified the producer lemma + sign computation; S16 (2026-06-15) added the Euler-side crux primitiveRoot_pow_half_eq_neg_one; S17 (2026-06-16) assembled the units-form Zolotarev headline legendreSym p (u.val) = sign(mulLeft u). overview.historicalContext: Zolotarev's lemma (1872) gives a strikingly different proof of Gauss's Law of Quadratic Reciprocity using the sign of a permutation. For an odd prime p and a coprime to p, the map x ↦ a·x is a permutation π_a of the nonzero residues (ZMod p)ˣ, and Zolotarev's lemma states that the Legendre symbol equals its sign: (a/p) = sign(π_a). Reciprocity then follows by computing the sign of a single 'grid transpose' permutation in two ways. The argument is purely combinatorial — no Gauss sums or quadratic forms — and is one of the cleanest routes to the 'golden theorem'. This entry formalizes the first milestone of that route: the group-theoretic engine that turns 'multiplication by a generator' into a cycle whose sign is computable.
overview.problemStatement: Formalize the permutation-sign (Zolotarev) route to quadratic reciprocity in Lean 4. The open question asks for an algorithmic/permutation-sign proof organized around Zolotarev's lemma. Milestone 1 (this entry): supply the reusable group-theoretic core — that left-multiplication by a generator of a finite group is a single cycle, and hence that sign(mulLeft (g^k)) = (-1)^k for even-order groups. This is the producer lemma Mathlib does not provide.
overview.proofStrategy: The producer lemma isCycle_mulLeft_of_generator discharges the IsCycle constructor with base point x = 1: mulLeft g moves 1 (since g ≠ 1, forced by generation plus card ≥ 2), and every y lies on the cycle of 1 because y ∈ zpowers g gives i with g^i = y, while (mulLeft g)^i applied to 1 equals g^i. The key wiring (mulLeft g)^i = mulLeft (g^i) is obtained from map_zpow applied to the inline monoid hom a ↦ Equiv.mulLeft a : G →* Perm G — Mathlib has no mulLeft_zpow/mulLeft_pow lemma at this pin, so the hom is bundled inline. Then sign_mulLeft_generator computes the sign: the support of mulLeft g is all of G (no fixed points since g ≠ 1), so IsCycle.sign gives sign = -(-1)^card, and card even collapses (-1)^card to 1, yielding -1. Finally sign_mulLeft_eq_neg_one_zpow factors mulLeft (g^k) = (mulLeft g)^k and uses that sign is a MonoidHom (map_zpow again) to get (-1)^k.
keyInsights: The single lemma Mathlib lacks is a PRODUCER, not a consumer: Mathlib proves what a cycle's sign and order are (IsCycle.sign, IsCycle.orderOf) but not that mulLeft by a generator IS a cycle. Isolating this is the genuinely-new content.

There is no mulLeft_zpow/mulLeft_pow lemma in Mathlib at rev 2df2f01; the clean substitute is to bundle a ↦ Equiv.mulLeft a as an inline monoid hom G →* Perm G and invoke map_zpow, which both IsCycle and sign computations reuse.

Evenness of the group order is exactly what makes the sign -1: a cycle of even length is an odd permutation. For (ZMod p)ˣ the order is p − 1, even for every odd prime, so Zolotarev's sign is always -1 on a generator.

The discrete-log form sign(mulLeft (g^k)) = (-1)^k is the bridge to Euler's criterion: with u = g^k, both the Legendre side (via legendreSym.eq_pow and the crux (g)^((p-1)/2) = -1) and the sign side reduce to (-1)^k, which is exactly how legendreSym_eq_sign_mulLeft now ties the two together for the units group.

The Euler-side crux is cleaner stated in the FIELD than in the units group: working with x = (g : ZMod p) lets the square-root-of-1 dichotomy use mul_self_eq_one_iff and ZMod.pow_card_sub_one_eq_one directly, sidestepping the units Neg-instance subtlety; (xᵐ)² = xᵖ⁻¹ = 1 with xᵐ ≠ 1 (since m < orderOf x = p−1) forces xᵐ = -1.

The final ±1 equality must be lifted from ZMod p back to ℤ, because legendreSym is ℤ-valued: the helper intCast_inj_pm exploits that 1 ≠ -1 in ZMod p for odd p (zmod_one_ne_neg_one) so the integer cast is injective on {1, -1}, completing legendreSym_eq_sign_mulLeft.

Because sign is a MonoidHom, the entire family of Zolotarev signs collapses to a single nontrivial computation: only sign(mulLeft g) = -1 on the generator must be evaluated by hand, and the value (-1)^k for every other element a = g^k follows for free by functoriality (map_zpow). This is why the proof is short despite covering all of (ZMod p)ˣ — there is essentially one sign to compute, not p−1 of them.

sections.summary: The import block pins exactly three Mathlib modules (LegendreSymbol.Basic, Perm.Cycle.Basic, SpecificGroups.Cyclic) plus Tactic at mathlib rev 2df2f01 (v4.26.0). The module docstring frames the permutation-sign (Zolotarev) route to quadratic reciprocity — (a/p) = sign(π_a) — and records the entry's epistemic status: machine-checked green in session S14 (first live-Docker session after S1–S13 were authored blind under an outage), 0 sorries / 0 axioms, with two re-runnable Python certificates (verify_zolotarev.py, verify_m1_cycle_lemma.py) corroborating the math build-free. It is explicit that this is Milestone 1 only: the headline identity and Milestone 2 are not yet formalized. Closes with the namespace and `open Equiv Equiv.Perm`.

sections.title: The Missing Producer Lemma
sections.summary: isCycle_mulLeft_of_generator: in a finite group of order ≥ 2 generated by g, left-multiplication by g is a single cycle. Discharges the IsCycle constructor at base point 1; the key step (mulLeft g)^i applied to 1 = g^i comes from map_zpow on an inline G →* Perm G monoid hom (Mathlib has no mulLeft_zpow at this pin).

sections.title: Sign of Multiplication by a Generator is −1
sections.summary: sign_mulLeft_generator: for an even-order finite group generated by g, sign (mulLeft g) = -1. The support is all of G (no fixed points since g ≠ 1), so IsCycle.sign gives -(-1)^card, and even card collapses (-1)^card to 1.

sections.title: Zolotarev Sign of an Arbitrary Element
sections.summary: sign_mulLeft_eq_neg_one_zpow: for a = g^k with g a generator of an even-order group, sign (mulLeft a) = (-1)^k. Factors mulLeft (g^k) = (mulLeft g)^k via the inline monoid hom + map_zpow, then uses sign being a MonoidHom. This is the Zolotarev sign side; combined with the crux below it gives the units-form headline.

sections.title: The Crux: Primitive Root to the (p−1)/2 Power is −1
sections.summary: primitiveRoot_pow_half_eq_neg_one (S16): for a generator g of (ZMod p)ˣ, (g : ZMod p)^((p-1)/2) = -1, the genuinely-new Euler-side ingredient. Stated in the FIELD ZMod p (not the units group) so the order-2 dichotomy uses mul_self_eq_one_iff directly: with x = (g : ZMod p) and m = (p-1)/2, (xᵐ)² = xᵖ⁻¹ = 1 (ZMod.pow_card_sub_one_eq_one) while xᵐ ≠ 1 (since m < orderOf x = p−1), so xᵐ = -1. This avoids the units Neg-instance subtlety flagged at S15.

sections.title: Units-Form Zolotarev Headline
sections.summary: legendreSym_eq_sign_mulLeft (S17): the units-form Zolotarev identity legendreSym p (u.val) = sign(mulLeft u) for u : (ZMod p)ˣ and odd prime p. Writing u = g^k for a generator g, the sign side gives (-1)^k via sign_mulLeft_eq_neg_one_zpow and the Legendre side gives (-1)^k via legendreSym.eq_pow plus the crux; the two ±1 integers are then identified by lifting the ZMod p equality back to ℤ through the private helpers intCast_inj_pm and zmod_one_ne_neg_one (which uses 1 ≠ -1 mod p for odd p). The exact OQ statement on the field via mulLeft₀ still needs the units→field sign bridge.

conclusion.summary: This entry machine-checks the permutation-sign (Zolotarev) route to quadratic reciprocity up through the units-form headline: the producer lemma that left-multiplication by a generator of a finite group is a single cycle (absent from Mathlib at rev 2df2f01), the sign computation sign(mulLeft (g^k)) = (-1)^k for even-order groups, the Euler-side crux that a primitive root of (ZMod p)ˣ raised to (p-1)/2 equals -1, and the units-form Zolotarev identity legendreSym p (u.val) = sign(mulLeft u). All results compile with zero sorries and zero axioms.
conclusion.implications: The producer lemma isCycle_mulLeft_of_generator is a reusable Mathlib-gap-filling result: it is the engine that makes Zolotarev's permutation-sign proof of quadratic reciprocity possible, and it applies to any finite cyclic group, not just (ZMod p)ˣ. Together with the Euler-side crux and the discrete-log sign computation it yields the units-form Zolotarev identity in full; what remains for a Gauss-sum-free proof of the whole reciprocity law is the units→field sign bridge (to reach the mulLeft₀ statement on ZMod p) and the grid-transpose sign computation of Milestone 2.
openQuestions: The verified headline is stated on the units group (ZMod p)ˣ via Equiv.mulLeft; the exact OQ-pinned statement uses Equiv.mulLeft₀ on the field ZMod p (which fixes 0). Deriving it requires the field-mulLeft₀ / units-mulLeft sign bridge (S2, numerically certified in knowledge.md but not yet in Lean).
Milestone 2 — deriving quadratic reciprocity itself from the sign of the grid-transpose permutation on (ZMod p)ˣ × (ZMod q)ˣ — is not yet in Lean.
Can the inline G →* Perm G monoid hom and a mulLeft_zpow lemma be contributed upstream to Mathlib, closing the producer gap for all future users?
